overall: Sound with fixes; not yet ready for the first real comparison. I re-ran the offline pipeline (three fake runs: headline 0.9613 for baseline, change-intent-v1 and change-intent-v1-frozen; diagnostics 0.0167 vs 0.6648; analyze.py shows zero differences with CIs), the hidden suite (seed 28 failed/4 passed, seed's own suite 17 passed, reference overlay 32 passed), and reproduced every mechanical claim both reviewers made in scratch repos and against the installed SDK/Harbor/Reward Kit sources. Of the first pass's 11 changes, 6 landed cleanly (1, 2, 7, 9, 11, and the SDK half of 6), 4 landed with residuals (3, 4, 8, 10), and 1 (5, the author stop rule) regressed: run_process.py:408 treats the intent as committed whenever `git log -- <intent_dir>` is non-empty, which is already true after the install commit adds `<intent_dir>/.gitkeep` at lines 379-381, so the dialogue ends the moment any draft file exists and the committed-contamination check at line 424 only inspects uncommitted paths. Both reviewers found this independently and I confirmed it (HEAD unmoved, log non-empty, `git status --porcelain` empty after an `add -A` commit that included a.py and notes.md). The other must-fix items before a real run are: the fixed reviewer's inputs are a subdirectory of the work dir that also holds the transcripts and process_review.md, and the harness commit message names the condition while fixed_reviewer.md tells the reviewer to run `git log`; the Harbor agent timeout (7200) equals the sum of the default stage caps with zero margin, copilot_process.py never passes --deadline-epoch, and summary_recorded spans every stage so only multi-stage conditions can lose handoff credit to a process-review hiccup; analyze.py never counts a reward-less trial in the local runs/ layout (reproduced n=1 miss=0 vs Harbor layout n=2 miss=1); and the harness implement prompt still says "the approved change intent" for every intent-bearing condition. Everything else is minor or belongs to the later 2x2 / shape-comparison work. On intent-like shapes: the schema already carries a single-file spec/ADR/plan in a directory (author.mode none/frozen/skill, prompt_file templates, intent.dir/claim_sections, neutral fixed reviewer); what is missing is a noun field, multi-file globs, an artifact produced by the implementer, and intent provenance in summary.json. A shape with no on-disk artifact is not supported because the implement stage is a fresh session, and that is the right boundary for this harness.
frame1_verdict: Does everything work without defect: sound with fixes. The offline path is solid and reproducible; every SDK 1.0.23 call site, event shape, and Harbor 0.24 / Reward Kit 0.2.3 contract the reviewers checked holds (I re-checked get_events awaited, abort/disconnect, _wait_for_structured_message's RuntimeError paths, excluded_tools/available_tools/additional_directories/skip_custom_instructions kwargs, _weighted_mean accepting weight 0, _subdirs skipping __hidden, to_thread + semaphore 8 for criteria, single_step running the verifier after AgentTimeoutError). Nothing prevents a run from starting; five defects would make its results untrustworthy (stop rule, committed contamination, reviewer sealing/commit messages, zero-margin timeout, analyze local-layout miss). One first-pass rejection (M1, assistant.usage ephemeral) was wrong: the pinned runtime 1.0.100's session-events.schema.json marks AssistantUsageEvent.ephemeral `const: true`; usage survives today only because the live capture list is longer than get_events().
frame2_verdict: Is the structure right to swap intent-construction and guidance variants: sound for baseline vs change-intent-v1 and for frozen-intent runs once the now-list lands; not yet sound for authoring-variant or shape comparisons. The process.json schema, sealed work dir, frozen mode with include_brief=false, and the diagnostics split are the right skeleton and I verified each works offline. The confounds that remain, in threat order: the stop rule (committed == exists), the stand-in's keyword approval (`final` anywhere in a question approves; confirmed), the harness implement prompt calling every artifact an "approved change intent", stage-count asymmetry in summary_recorded and the Harbor timeout, the fixed reviewer's visibility of condition identity, and committed contamination. For the 2x2 (skills x guidances with frozen intents) the harness also lacks the intent factor in summary.json (only basename + sha), an author-only stop, grouping by label in analyze.py, and a Harbor route for --intent-file. These are real but are not needed before baseline vs v1; they are needed before any claim about which skill writes better intents.

changes_now.title: Author stage: stop on a real commit, catch committed contamination, fix agent_committed, drop the 'final' approval cue

Implement stage: read head_after_agent = git_head(ws) BEFORE git_commit_all and set agent_committed = head_after_agent != head_before_impl. stand_in.py:_freeform: remove 'final' from the approval cues (keep 'approve', 'ready for approval', 'proposed intent') and record which cue fired in the Exchange. Add an offline test (e.g. driver/test_author_stage.py run by run_local.sh or pytest) that drives intent_state/next_author_turn through: no file -> uncommitted draft -> stand-in asks for the file once -> approval -> commit -> None; and a FakeBackend variant that writes the draft before asking, so the regression cannot recur silently.
changes_now.why: Today committed == exists, so the dialogue ends the first time a skill writes a draft, the harness commits unapproved drafts, author_outcome labels are wrong in one direction, and anything the author committed outside the intent dir (code, scratch files) silently becomes part of the intent commit and the implementation baseline. All of that lands in the change-intent condition only, so a score difference would partly measure when the skill touches disk and how it commits, not intent quality. The 'final' cue approves drafts nobody has seen.

changes_now.title: Time budget, handoff scoping, structured-output retry, and a verified read-only tool set
changes_now.what: task.toml: [agent] timeout_sec = 9000. copilot_process.py: prepend `start=$(date +%s);` to the command and pass `--deadline-epoch $((start + 7800))` so the driver always finishes, resets and copies before Harbor's deadline; also pass caps unchanged. criteria.summary_recorded: require summary present, no harness_error, and status ok / not timed_out for the 'implement' and 'fixed_review' stages only; report author/review stage status as a new diagnostics criterion (process_stages_clean). backends.run_stage: when response_schema is set and send_and_wait raises RuntimeError whose message starts with 'Run completed without a structured assistant response' (or parse_review_json fails on the result), send one follow-up turn 'Return only the JSON object matching the schema, nothing else.' before giving up; record retries in StageResult/summary. Read-only stages: replace the guessed excluded_tools list with available_tools = ['grep', 'glob', 'view', 'bash', 'read_bash', 'stop_bash', 'lsp'], which is the read-only set the pinned runtime's own explore.agent.yaml declares (definitions/explore.agent.yaml in cli/1.0.100), and note in the README that this was taken from the bundle; keep the reset-and-record safety net.
changes_now.why: 7200 == sum of caps gives zero margin for session start-up, abort/get_events, git and the copy; only multi-stage conditions can hit it, and when they do /app/.eval is never written, so handoff and review go to zero asymmetrically. summary_recorded today lets a process-review hiccup (which feeds only diagnostics) cost change-intent conditions 1/14 of the headline while baseline has no such stage. A single reviewer formatting slip removes ~0.36 of a trial's reward with no retry, which at k=3 can swamp the effect. The excluded_tools names ('edit', 'create', 'write', 'apply_patch', 'multi_edit') are unconfirmed against the runtime; available_tools from the bundled read-only agent is confirmed and takes precedence in the SDK.

changes_later.title: Review rubric decisions (owner): verdict calibration, intent in diff.patch, reviewer tampering flag
changes_later.what: (a) reviewer_verdict_correct -> agreement with ground truth: 1.0 when verdict=correct and hidden_tests_all_pass or verdict=incorrect and not all pass, 0.5 uncertain, else 0; keep 'reviewer convinced' as a diagnostic. (b) intent.in_diff (default false): generate diff.patch with `:(exclude)<intent_dir>` since the artifact is already in change_description.md; keep both shortstats. (c) analyze.py flags trials whose fixed_review.reset_paths/head_moved is non-empty and reports the review dimension with and without them. Because review.json and the workspace are kept, the review group can be re-graded offline, so this can be decided after the first run without rerunning it; deciding before is cleaner.
changes_later.why: As scored, a confident description can raise the verdict without being more correct, and size/effort are judged on a diff that includes the artifact and the extra tests the guidance mandates, so the sign of a review-dimension difference is hard to interpret.

changes_later.title: Multi-file and implementer-produced artifacts
changes_later.what: intent: {files: [globs] (default ['<dir>/*.md']), produced_by: author|implement (default author)}. Resolve after the producing stage; embed every matched file in change_description.md under its path; intent_file_present becomes 'at least one' with the count recorded; copy matched files into work/intent/.
changes_later.why: A spec split across files, an ADR plus plan, or a plan the implementer writes first cannot be run or is mis-described today (find_intent takes the alphabetically last *.md). Needed for shape comparisons, not for baseline vs v1.

changes_later.title: Per-stage agents_block
changes_later.what: Allow agents_block to be a map {author, implement, review}; rewrite and commit AGENTS.md before each stage. Until then, document that guidance ablations must use frozen intents (where the author stage does not run and the single block is clean).
changes_later.why: A 'guidance off' cell in a non-frozen cross either keeps the mandate via AGENTS.md or changes the authoring input too.

changes_later.title: Fixed reviewer and AGENTS.md (owner decision)
changes_later.what: Either leave AGENTS.md in the tree (custom instructions are off; it is part of what the process leaves behind) and add a diagnostic that scans events-fixed_review.json for a view/bash read of AGENTS.md or the intent dir, or review in a `git worktree` of impl_commit with AGENTS.md restored to the seed version. Default: leave it for the first run with the diagnostic, revisit if the reviewer reads it.
changes_later.why: Reading AGENTS.md would pull change-intent review rules into change-intent trials only; the frequency is unknown until a real run.

changes_later.title: Event merge by id instead of 'longer list wins'
changes_later.what: backends.run_stage: merge get_events() and live_events by event id, preferring the live payload; compute usage and resolved_model from the merged list. Note in the README that assistant.usage is ephemeral in runtime 1.0.100.
changes_later.why: Usage currently survives because the live list is always longer; a merge removes the dependence on that accident.

changes_later.title: Small offline hygiene
changes_later.what: criteria._pytest_cached: a threading.Lock per key so the hidden suite truly runs once. run_local.sh: match --backend=fake and point --fake-reference at a directory containing only ledger/ (or skip *.sh). Diagram 03 and README step 3: regenerate after the stop-rule fix so they describe the code.
changes_later.why: Quality and clarity; no effect on the comparison.

changes_later.title: Stand-in approval detection: structural instead of keyword
changes_later.what: Approve only when the agent's message contains the artifact's heading pattern (any of intent.required_sections as `## ` headings, or a fenced block) and ends with a question; move any residual cue list to process.json (author.approval_cues). Record the triggering rule in author_dialogue.json.
changes_later.why: The stand-in should be the constant across authoring variants; keyword cues make author_outcome a function of each skill's vocabulary. Dropping 'final' (now-list) removes the worst case; the structural rule is for the authoring 2x2.

Inspected the fake v1 run: .eval listing (review-input beside transcripts and process_review.md), git log ('eval: install process change-intent-v1'), agent_committed True with no agent commit, rendered fixed-review prompt with the mkdtemp path and differing SHA across two runs, implement prompt 'the approved change intent at ...', diff.patch including solve.sh and the intent file. Installed sources: copilot/session.py get_events (3692), _wait_for_structured_message (2410-2441, RuntimeError on empty final message), abort (3770); client.py create_session kwargs and toolFilterPrecedence 'excluded'; _cli_version.py CLI_VERSION 1.0.100; runtime bundle cli/1.0.100 schemas/session-events.schema.json AssistantUsageEvent.ephemeral const true; definitions/explore.agent.yaml read-only tool list (grep, glob, view, bash, read_bash, stop_bash, powershell..., lsp); the code-review agent uses tools '*' so edit-tool names remain unconfirmed. harbor/trial/trial.py 651-657 (wait_for around run only), single_step.py 76-86 (verifier after AgentTimeoutError); rewardkit reward.py 50-54 (_weighted_mean, 0 weight fine), 345 (to_thread), runner.py 253 (_subdirs skips '.'/'__'), 716 (max_concurrent_programmatic=8); installed harbor_rewardkit 0.2.3.

Trade-offs for the owner, with my default: (1) reviewer_verdict_correct as 'reviewer convinced' vs agreement with hidden tests: default agreement (it measures whether the description let the reviewer tell), keep convinced as diagnostic; can be regraded offline. (2) Intent file inside diff.patch: default exclude (the reviewer has it in change_description.md; size/effort then measure code), record both shortstats as today. (3) AGENTS.md visible to the fixed reviewer: default leave for the first run with a read-detection diagnostic. (4) Harbor timeout: raise to 9000 with --deadline-epoch +7800 rather than cutting the implement cap, so the implement budget stays identical and generous across conditions. (5) Read-only stages: available_tools from the bundled explore agent rather than guessed excluded_tools; bash stays because the reviewer must run tests, and the reset-and-record net stays. (6) Stand-in approval: drop 'final' now; structural detection before the authoring 2x2. (7) summary_recorded scope: implement + fixed_review only; author/review stage health to diagnostics. The first pass's decision to still implement on no_file and report ITT/per-protocol separately stands and is not reopened.

Intent-like shapes: a single-file spec, ADR or plan in a directory already fits (author.mode none/frozen/skill, prompt_file, intent.dir/claim_sections/required_sections, neutral fixed reviewer); with change 5 the harness stops calling it a change intent. Multi-file artifacts, an artifact the implementer writes, and an artifact that is not a file are not supported; the first two are the later-list schema items, the third is out of scope by construction (fresh implement session) and should be documented as such rather than bolted on.

Not reported as new findings: the deferred items in README (intent-isolation protocol, hidden author preferences, direct intent grader/mutants, blinded diff-only arm, more tasks, separately pinned stand-in model, digest-pinned images). None is needed before the first run.
